mainEntity.name: What is an insider cluster buy?

acceptedAnswer.text: An insider cluster buy happens when two or more distinct company insiders report qualifying purchases of the same stock within a rolling detection window. InsiderClusters groups these purchases so you can research the buyers, dates, and amounts together.

mainEntity.name: Where does the insider buying data come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our data comes from public SEC Form 4 filings on EDGAR. Each transaction links to its original filing so you can check the price, shares, ownership details, and footnotes yourself.

mainEntity.name: Does insider buying mean a stock will go up?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Insider buying is a research input, not a prediction of returns. Clusters can help you identify companies to investigate, but prices can fall and filings may have important context in their footnotes.

mainEntity.name: When will I receive an alert?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pro includes email and Telegram alerts when our monitoring detects a new qualifying cluster. Alerts follow public filing and processing, not the moment a trade takes place. Basic includes the cluster feed and a weekly email digest.

mainEntity.name: How does the free trial work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both plans begin with a 7-day free trial. A card is required at checkout. You are charged after the trial unless you cancel before it ends. Annual billing is also available at checkout.

schema_present_in_response.headline: Form 4 transaction codes explained (P, S, A, M, F, G…)
schema_present_in_response.description: Every SEC Form 4 transaction carries a one-letter code. P and S are the ones that matter for signal — here's the full table and what each code actually means.

mainEntity.name: What does transaction code P mean on a Form 4?

acceptedAnswer.text: Code P reports an open-market or private purchase. Read the ownership details, plan designation, and footnotes to understand who bought and under what circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What does transaction code A mean on a Form 4?

acceptedAnswer.text: Code A marks a grant or award of shares from the company. It is compensation, not a buying decision, so it carries no signal about the insider's outlook.

mainEntity.name: Which Form 4 codes indicate real insider buying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only code P reflects a voluntary purchase with the insider's own money; codes A, M, F, G, C, D, and X describe compensation or administrative events.

body_excerpt: Form 4 transaction codes explained (P, S, A, M, F, G…) | InsiderClusters Skip to content Insider Clusters Stocks Insiders Sectors Archive Learn Pricing Sign in Start free trial ↗ Home / Learn / Form 4 transaction codes explained (P, S, A, M, F, G…) Form 4 transaction codes explained (P, S, A, M, F, G…) By InsiderClusters · Updated 2026-10-12 · Sources & methodology In this guide The codes that matter ↓ Why we only track code P ↓ Every transaction reported on a SEC Form 4 carries a single-letter code describing how the insider acquired or disposed of the shares. Most codes describe administrative events — compensation, taxes, transfers. Only a couple describe an insider making a real market decision with real money, which is why filtering by code is the first step in any insider-trading analysis. The codes that matter Code Meaning Signal value P Open-market or private purchase A purchase; verify ownership and context in the footnotes S Open-market or private sale Weak negative — insiders sell for taxes, diversification, houses A Grant or award from the company None — it's compensation, not a decision M Option or derivative exercise None by itself — often paired with a same-day S F Shares withheld to pay tax on vesting None — automatic, not discretionary G Bona fide gift None — estate planning, charity C Conversion of a derivative security None — mechanical D Disposition back to the company None — usually plan-related X Exercise of in-the-money options at expiry None — forced by the calendar J Other (described in a footnote) Read the footnote — occasionally interesting Why we only track code P A code- P purchase is the only routine Form 4 event where an insider voluntarily converts personal cash into more exposure to their own company. Codes A , M , and F dominate filing volume but carry no intent at all — counting them as "insider buying" is the most common mistake in DIY Form 4 analysis.
